_comment: Two caps for two different things. max_survivor_fraction is a one-sided cap on the SAMPLED run's survivor rate (saturable: below 1.0, because a rate in [0,1] can never exceed 1.0). unpinned_sites is the exact-count ratchet over the DETERMINISTIC inventory -- every candidate site the six operators generate across the whole tree -- and only moves down: a diff that adds a candidate site without a disposition raises it and is refused. A site carries a disposition under survivor_triage (a verdict) or killed_by (a driver that kills it). See the header of tests/mutation_table.py.

reason: max_survivor_fraction was OPEN at 1.0 and therefore unsatisfiable: rate = survivors/evaluated is a fraction in [0,1], so `if rate > 1.0` can never fire and a run in which every mutant survives printed PASSED. The caps are now recorded at the last measured rates -- 0.2 (2 survivors of 10) and 0.3 (12 of 40) -- so they are saturable. The ratchet is the exact-count `unpinned_sites`: 3798 candidate sites enumerated deterministically over all 64 production modules, of which 3785 carry no recorded disposition (3 are triaged equivalent: pump_mode.py:242, __init__.py:340, optimizer.py:3565; 10 are killed -- 7 by tests/features.py: battery.py:320, battery.py:341, defrost.py:166, defrost.py:169, defrost.py:171, defrost.py:172, thermal_model.py:1894, and 3 by tests/entities.py: sensor.py:427, sensor.py:430, sensor.py:432 -- recorded under `killed_by`). The two surviving sites the disposition pass measured -- defrost.py:310 GUARD_OFF and sysid.py:1522 GUARD_OFF, both added with origin/main -- stay unpinned on purpose: nothing in the recorded driver net kills them yet, and an unmarked survivor is a gap rather than an equivalence. The nightly burn-in kills or triages them in cost order, and each disposition must name the mechanism; the ratchet refuses any NEW site without one. Do not raise `unpinned_sites` by hand: the exact count is re-derived every run by tests/mutation_table.py, which refuses growth and only records down via --record.
